subject.title: Sub-agent startup silence: no first-progress signal, aborted runs appear as hangs

question: Should OpenClaw add the proposed `first-progress` and typed `startup-failed` lifecycle phases to core, or solve sub-agent startup silence through a narrower existing-status/diagnostic path?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the requested repair adds a new core lifecycle event contract that affects gateway, session, SDK, and subagent consumers; automation should not choose that API shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor current-main lifecycle contract
options.body: Accept the new lifecycle semantics and replace the stale PR with a current-main implementation that wires the phases through embedded-agent, subagent registry, gateway wait/session projection, SDK normalization, docs, and focused proof.

options.title: Narrow to existing status diagnostics
options.body: Decline new phases for now and fix the hang perception by preserving startup abort attribution in existing end/error/status paths plus user-visible diagnostics.

options.title: Defer API surface
options.body: Keep the issue open but blocked until maintainers define a broader agent lifecycle event model that can absorb this and related lifecycle requests.

recommendation.title: Sponsor current-main lifecycle contract
recommendation.body: Accept the new lifecycle semantics and replace the stale PR with a current-main implementation that wires the phases through embedded-agent, subagent registry, gateway wait/session projection, SDK normalization, docs, and focused proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to subagent lifecycle stabilization and registry lifecycle ownership as the central decision surface for the API shape.
